newsitem.title: USA: Sino-US ag trade outlook better - USDA's Glickman.
newsitem.headline: Sino-US ag trade outlook better - USDA's Glickman.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Tuesday that he believed chances had improved for resolving U.S.-China farm trade disputes.

President Clinton raised agricultural trade issues during a meeting with the Chinese president last weekend, said Glickman, who attended the session held on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Manila.
"He mentioned particularly agriculture (as an area) that he wanted additional (market) access," Glickman told reporters.
No commitments were made during the meeting but Glickman said its tone was encouraging.
"I viewed that the picture was a lot brighter in terms of resolution of trade disputes" in agriculture, Glickman said.

The United States contends China has unfairly restricted imports of U.S. wheat on grounds of concern over the TCK smut fungus. There also have been recent disagreements over poultry sales and a threat by China to temporarily ban some U.S. agricultural goods in retaliation for U.S. sanctions in a textile dispute.
